request.outcome: Provide native CSS paint-time ellipsis at word boundaries for text-overflow.
request.status_reason: The follow-up says line-clamp already specifies the requested behavior; text-overflow remains different. Other cross-referenced discussions are not acquired, so current resolution is not established.

requirements.text: Handle native CSS text-overflow paint-time rendering, not server-side string shortening.
requirements.quote: `text-overflow` is a paint time effect over overflowing content, not a truncation of content.

requirements.text: Only allow clipping at word boundaries.
requirements.quote: Having an option to only allow clipping at word boundaries can eliminate this problem.

environment: Browser CSS layout, paint-time ellipsis, widths and scrolling.
prior_attempts: The collaborator clarifies that line-clamp already clips at soft wrapping opportunities.
missing_information: Current disposition of cross-referenced CSSWG discussions.

matches.summary: The phrase 'word boundaries' retrieves a similar mechanism, but a Python character-count helper cannot implement native CSS paint/layout semantics.

checks.reason: smart_truncate receives a Python string and integer max_length, selects words using string splitting, and returns a string. It has no browser layout widths, scroll state or CSS property implementation. Server-side text alteration would change the requested mechanism.
Its ordinary character-budget truncation is not pixel/paint-time clipping, and it also has hard-slice fallback edges.

obstacles: Hard runtime/layout mismatch: Python string processing versus browser-native CSS behavior.
The line-clamp branch is not an unmet need according to the follow-up.
A new browser layout implementation would be a different project, not narrow reuse.

bridge.summary: Do not propose python-slugify as the solution; retain the rejection and CSS context.
steps: Consult the linked CSSWG discussion and the collaborator's distinction between line-clamp and text-overflow.
Only reevaluate if the demand changes to explicit server-side plain-text shortening.
bridge.existing_contribution: No compatible contribution to the mandatory native CSS behavior.
bridge.new_logic: Browser-native layout/paint work would be a substantial new implementation, not an adapter.
